other_stage_coverage.rule: P07 coverage is NOT P06 coverage. It is recorded so the residual risk is scoped accurately, never to claim the P06 family is covered.

noisy_diagnosis.structural_cause: Not one of the 10 NOISY-tagged submissions has a single resolvable P06 property. Injection-resistance properties assert a cross-cutting stage obligation -- do not obey instruction-shaped text inside the submission -- rather than a claim about a named rubric criterion. A construct-named P06 gate therefore cannot carry them at all. This is a property-genre mismatch, not a resolver accident, and no resolver change closes it.

A04_S03_P1_bound_to_wrong_construct.note: The property is about the rubric distinction 'No verificable' vs 'No'. The bare token 'No' resolved by UNIQUE_NAME_PREFIX to the one A04 criterion whose name begins 'No ...'.

A04_S05_P5_multi_verification_mismatch.note: The property asserts two checklist verifications. Only the exact one matched; the paraphrase was discarded in silence.

copied_key_alignment_is_tautological.note: Both fields are written from the same resolver variable in the same loop iteration, so construct_identity_equal cannot be false.

p07_has_no_field_authority_or_companion.note: The generic packet exposes the materialized output and an opaque opportunity id. Nothing told a blind reviewer which fields the provider owned.

applied_to_frozen_v12.note: v1.2 reported every one of these rows as aligned. The independent verifier disagrees, which is the evidence that it is not the same tautology.

phase_d_rare_coverage.substitution_rule: PROMPT_INJECTION_SILENT coverage is never evidence of PROMPT_INJECTION_NOISY coverage. Resisting a quiet injected instruction and resisting a loud one are separate observable behaviours, and only the family actually exercised may be claimed.

A_existing_corpus_fixture_or_binding_cov.evidence: Every UNCERTAIN-asserting property fails the one-construct gate: most name no rubric criterion because they assert UNCERTAIN about the submission as a whole or about everything that would depend on an absent artifact; A07-S02-P2 names two criteria exactly; A04-S03-P1 asserts over the four rows of the 'Nota técnica' rubric section at once.

B_corpus_semantic_coverage.evidence: The frozen corpus asserts UNCERTAIN in 9 submission-level P06 properties across 6 activities, 8 of them with oracle_state VALID and kind REQUIRED. A further 2 activity-level P06 properties describe UNCERTAIN as a coverage index over their activity's submissions, which is not a candidate gate; both scopes together are 11 properties. Of the submission-level population, 0 reach an executable candidate-scoring route. The material exists; it cannot be routed.

C_production_contract_expressiveness.evidence: EvidenceSupportStatus admits UNCERTAIN, and EvidenceMappingRelationDraft exposes support_status, semantic_uncertainty and abstention_reason. Production can express the behaviour the benchmark cannot currently observe.

activity_level_describing_uncertain.rule: An activity-level property states which P06 states the activity offers across its submissions. It is a coverage index over the activity, not a claim a candidate can be scored against, and it must never be counted as though it were a gate.

candidate_scoring_executable_asserting_u.rule: A submission-level property that reached an executable route with oracle_state VALID. Only this population can be observed by a qualification run.

combined_both_scopes.rule: Reported only with the scope stated. This number is the size of the corpus material that touches UNCERTAIN at any scope; it is not a population of candidate gates.

census.scope_rule: Every count states its scope. A submission-level candidate-gate population is never summed with an activity-wide coverage-index statement without saying so.
